```{r}
#| label: plots
#| include: false
width_cols <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3")
plot_interval_widths <- c(0.5, 0.95)
plot_levels <- join_and(fmt_pct(plot_interval_widths, 0))
if (requireNamespace("paletteer", quietly = TRUE)) {
  width_cols <- tryCatch(as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("RColorBrewer::Dark2"))[1:3], error = function(e) width_cols)
}
lab_ms <- function(v) ifelse(v >= 1000, sprintf("%.1f s", v / 1000), sprintf("%.3g ms", v))

# A statistic with a cuplyr cell that was not timed (CPU fallback) carries the
# note as a caption on its plot, and as a row in its table.
skip_fns <- function(stat) unique(sk_main$fn[sk_main$stat == stat & grepl("^cuplyr", sk_main$fn)])

# the caption of a statistic's plot: one note per untimed cuplyr entry,
# wrapped so a long note stays inside the figure
plot_caption <- function(stat) {
  if (!length(skip_fns(stat))) return(NULL)
  paste(vapply(skip_fns(stat), function(f) paste(strwrap(paste0(f, " ", skip_note(stat, f)), width = 90), collapse = "\n"), ""), collapse = "\n")
}
plot_height <- function(stat) {
  d <- main[main$stat == stat, ]
  cap <- plot_caption(stat)
  2 + 0.55 * length(unique(d$fn)) + 0.2 * if (is.null(cap)) 0 else length(strsplit(cap, "\n")[[1]])
}

stat_plot <- function(stat) {
  d <- main[main$stat == stat, ]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(invisible(NULL))
  med_mid <- tapply(d$ms[d$width == w_mid], d$fn[d$width == w_mid], stats::median)
  ord <- names(sort(med_mid, decreasing = TRUE))
  ord <- c(setdiff(unique(d$fn), ord), ord)
  d$fn <- factor(d$fn, levels = ord)
  d$width_f <- factor(d$width)
  lab <- data.frame(fn = factor(names(med_mid), levels = ord), ms = as.numeric(med_mid), label = lab_ms(as.numeric(med_mid)))
  sub <- paste0("point = median, bars = ", paste(fmt_pct(plot_interval_widths, 0), collapse = " / "), " of samples; label = median at width ", w_mid, "\n",
                "(1 thread) = same call with that package's thread count set to 1\n",
                "cuplyr: computation only, data already on the GPU, no upload/download")
  cap <- plot_caption(stat)
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x = ms, y = fn, colour = width_f))
  if (requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    p <- p + ggdist::stat_pointinterval(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.6), .width = plot_interval_widths, point_size = 1.8)
  } else {
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_boxplot(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.6), width = 0.5)
  }
  p +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = lab, ggplot2::aes(x = ms, y = fn, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.35, size = 3) +
    # room on the right for the label of the slowest entry
    ggplot2::scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                           expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.22))) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = width_cols, name = "window width") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "time per call, ms (log10)", y = NULL,
                  title = paste0("Rolling ", stat, ", n = ", format(n_rows, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")), subtitle = sub, caption = cap) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
                   plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0, face = "bold"),
                   panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

ext_sub <- "computation only, data already on the GPU (cuplyr); no upload/download.\nBars/points = median; error bars = IQR; (1 thread) = threads set to 1"
ext_panels <- function() {
  d1 <- ext[ext$experiment == "grouped mean", ]
  d2 <- ext[ext$experiment != "grouped mean", ]
  d2$one_thread <- grepl("1 thread", d2$fn)
  panels <- list()
  if (nrow(d1)) panels[[1]] <- ggplot2::ggplot(d1, ggplot2::aes(x = median_ms, y = stats::reorder(fn, -median_ms))) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = width_cols[1]) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(xmin = q25_ms, xmax = q75_ms), width = 0.2, orientation = "y") +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = lab_ms(median_ms)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "median ms (IQR bars)", y = NULL,
                  title = paste0("Grouped rolling mean, ", format(group_rows, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ","), " rows, ", n_groups, " groups, w = ", group_width),
                  subtitle = ext_sub) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + ggplot2::theme(plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
  if (nrow(d2)) panels[[length(panels) + 1]] <- ggplot2::ggplot(d2, ggplot2::aes(x = width, y = median_ms, colour = fn, group = fn, linetype = one_thread)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "dashed"), guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_log10(breaks = unique(d2$width)) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "window width (log10)", y = "median ms (log10)", colour = NULL,
                  title = paste0("Ungrouped rolling mean, ", format(ext_rows, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ","), " rows"), subtitle = ext_sub) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
  panels
}
ext_plot <- function() patchwork::wrap_plots(ext_panels(), ncol = 1)
ext_plot_height <- 3.4 * length(ext_panels()) + 0.5

# ---- tables -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
cell_txt <- function(stat, fn, width) {
  i <- cell_i(stat, fn, width)
  if (!is.na(i)) return(sprintf("%s (%s-%s) n=%d", fmt_ms(cells$med[i]), fmt_ms(cells$q25[i]), fmt_ms(cells$q75[i]), cells$n[i]))
  if (width %in% skip_widths(stat, fn)) return("not timed (CPU fallback)")
  if (any(cr$stat == stat & cr$fn == fn & cr$width == width & grepl("^error:", cr$note))) return("error (see Correctness)")
  ""
}
stat_table <- function(stat) {
  fns <- unique(c(cells$fn[cells$stat == stat], cr$fn[cr$stat == stat]))
  if (!length(fns) && !length(skip_fns(stat))) return(invisible(NULL))
  fns <- fns[order(vapply(fns, function(f) med(stat, f, w_mid), 0))]
  out <- data.frame(`function` = fns, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (w in widths) out[[paste0("w=", w)]] <- vapply(fns, function(f) cell_txt(stat, f, w), "")
  # cuplyr entries that were not timed at any width: a row saying so, not a
  # number (a partial skip shows in the entry's own row)
  for (f in setdiff(skip_fns(stat), fns)) {
    out[nrow(out) + 1, ] <- c(f, skip_note(stat, f), rep("not timed", length(widths) - 1))
  }
  knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

Redo of <https://roald-arboel.com/blog/posts/2024/10/03/Benchmark-rolling/> with cuplyr added as one more entry in every statistic panel, and polars and DuckDB added as further entries (Theo, 2026-10-25) at their default threads and at one thread. The rendered report is published at `r file.path(params$out_dir, "rolling-window.html")`. Produced by this document (`bench/rolling-window.qmd`; helpers in `bench/rolling-lib.R`, installs in `bench/install-deps.R`): the code that produces every number, table and figure is in the same file as the prose, and every number in the prose is computed from the results. Raw data, written to `r params$out_dir` on every render: `timings.csv`, `correctness.csv`, `extension.csv`, `versions.csv`, `memory-breakdown.csv`, `memory-finding.csv`, `skipped.csv`, `engine-threads.csv``r if (is.null(bench_cores$timings)) "" else ", \x60cores.csv\x60 (the core-placement samples)"`.

**Run configuration:** cell budget `r cell_budget` s, probe limit `r probe_limit` s, `times` `r times`, `times_custom` `r times_c`, `ext_times` `r ext_times`. `r cfg_txt`. See "How to render" at the end for the command.

Wall time of the timing chunks, which hold the GPU: **`r fmt_dur(wall_secs)`** (`r paste0(names(secs_by_chunk), " ", fmt_dur(secs_by_chunk), collapse = ", ")`; `r wall_origin_txt`). Every number below is computed in this document from those results.

## Read this first: what the numbers are

**What cuplyr's number is.** The cuplyr timing is the **computation on a table that is already on the GPU**: `res <- compute(mutate(gt, r = roll_mean(x, n)))` followed by `gpu_sync()` as a fence, with `gt <- tbl_gpu(df)` built once outside timing. By decision (Theo, 2026-10-21) it contains **no upload and no `collect()`**. The post's CPU packages operate on an R vector already in memory, and polars and DuckDB on their own in-engine copy of the data (next paragraph), so every entry times the computation only. A real pipeline that starts and ends in R would also pay the PCIe transfers that are excluded here (not measured in this study). `r only_native_txt`

**What the CPU numbers are: measured thread behaviour, not settings.** Package thread settings do not say what a call did, so each multi-thread-capable entry (data.table, RcppRoll, roll, and the engines polars and DuckDB) was timed twice, at its default setting and with its threads set to one (entries labelled `(1 thread)`), and the "Threads actually used" section reports both. The result:

- **RcppRoll `r rr_runs` `r n_rr_threads` OpenMP threads by default** (`RcppRoll::roll_threads()` = `r n_rr_threads`) and `r rr_claim`.
- **`r dt_lead`** (default vs `setDTthreads(1)` within `r dt_within`), although `getDTthreads()` is `r n_dt_threads`. `r dt_only` `r dt_weak_txt`
- **`r roll_lead`** `r roll_claim`. `r roll_omp_txt`
- `r join_and(unctl)` were not given a thread control. `r unctl_check`
- `r eng_reading("polars")`
- `r eng_reading("DuckDB")`

So there is no blanket "GPU against N CPU threads" framing in this report: the comparison is to the per-entry thread behaviour above. Medians are reported with their spread (IQR in the tables, all samples in `timings.csv`). No headline speedup is claimed.

**What the polars and DuckDB numbers are.** polars and DuckDB follow the same rule as cuplyr: each engine gets its data once, outside timing, and the timed call is only the rolling computation, to a result that stays inside the engine. For polars the timed call is `pdf$with_columns(<rolling expression>$alias("r"))` on a polars DataFrame built once (eager, so the expression is evaluated when the call returns; `over("g")` when grouped), and the result is never converted to R inside timing. For DuckDB it is one `CREATE TEMP TABLE rw_out AS SELECT i, <guarded window aggregate> AS r FROM rw_x WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY i ROWS BETWEEN n - 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)` on an in-memory DuckDB table loaded once; the result is materialized inside DuckDB and nothing is fetched into R. The sort that `ORDER BY i` implies is inside the timed query, because SQL has no row order without it. That is "closest to computation only" for DuckDB: fetching the result into R would add a copy that cuplyr's timing does not have either. Both engines ran at their default threads (polars `r eng_default_thr[["polars"]]`, DuckDB `r eng_default_thr[["DuckDB"]]`, read back from the engine) and at one thread (polars `r eng_one_thr[["polars"]]`, DuckDB `r eng_one_thr[["DuckDB"]]`). The comparison with cuplyr is therefore engine against GPU on in-engine data, not against an R vector.

**What the cuplyr number still includes, per call.** R dispatch of `mutate()`/`compute()`, the AST node builds and schema inference, lowering to C++, the `r words(n_mat_win)` nodes of an eager window `mutate()` (`r node_list`), `r chain_share_txt` (see "Per-call cost breakdown"), and the fence. The same call on a `r small_txt`-row table, where kernel time is negligible, takes about `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms for window functions (a plain `mutate(y = x + 1)` takes `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms). That floor is `r floor_share_txt` and `r floor_vs_dt` the whole data.table call (`r fmt_ms(med("mean", "data.table", w_mid))` ms). The `r alloc_part` part grows with the row count and is **inside every `r rows_txt` and `r ext_txt` cuplyr timing** but not in the `r small_txt`-row floor. `r eng_floor_txt`

## Method

- Data: `rw_data(n)` (`set.seed(12345)` by default, then `rnorm(n)`) with n = `r rows_txt`, no NAs, widths `r widths_slash`, right-aligned, output the same length as the input, `NA` padded. Same functions and arguments as the post (see `rw_functions()` in `bench/rolling-lib.R`), `times` = `r times`, `times` = `r times_c` for the custom function.
- **Deviation 1, one harness for everyone.** The post used `microbenchmark(times = 20)`, which interleaves expressions and does not force a GC. Here every function (CPU packages, polars, DuckDB and cuplyr) goes through `rw_time()`: untimed warmup calls, then `times` samples; an untimed `gc()` runs before every call with the previous result already dropped; each sample is timed with `microbenchmark::get_nanotime()`. `r gc_lead`: `r gc_why_txt` (finding F1), and `r gc_need_txt`. Applying the same `gc()` to everyone keeps the comparison symmetric. Consequence: no GC ever lands inside a timed region, which in the post's interleaved harness it sometimes did, and deallocation of each result is untimed for every engine (`r free_txt`; the CPU packages' vectors and polars' DataFrames likewise; DuckDB's result table is dropped by the untimed `reset`). A test (`tests/testthat/test-bench-F54-harness-extra.R`) pins that `gc()` runs before every call and outside the timed region.
- **Deviation 2, GPU completion.** cuplyr's API gives no "work finished" guarantee (`r sync_txt`). The timed closure ends with `cuplyr::gpu_sync()`, which waits for all queued GPU work (no copy back to the host). The fence adds `r fence_cost` (chunk `bench-fence` timed `r fence_txt`); the call without the fence returns once the work is queued, so it times the launch only, and the difference is the GPU time the fence waits for.
- **Deviation 3, slow cells get fewer samples** (`cell_budget` = `r cell_budget` s of timed work per cell). Each cell starts with one cold probe call; its duration sets the sample count through `rw_plan_cell()` (`bench/rolling-lib.R`). A cuplyr cell has one more untimed call before that one, the native probe of the fallback check below, so its "cold" call is its second call and it gets one more warm-up call than the CPU packages. The probe call is *not* a recorded sample (unless it alone exceeds `probe_limit` = `r probe_limit` s, `r probe_txt`); warmup calls (`r warmup_txt`) and then `k` timed calls follow, and the `note` column of `timings.csv` records exactly this per cell. Every cut is listed in the `times` cuts table.
- **Deviation 4, runstats alignment moved out of timing.** `runstats::RunningMean/RunningSd` return left-aligned windows (the window starts at i; the last `n - 1` values are `NA`). The timed closure returns that raw result and only tags it in place (`attr(out, "rw_align") <- "left"`, plus the window width in `rw_window`, on the local fresh vector: no copy). `rw_normalize()` shifts tagged output to right-aligned, outside timing, before the correctness check. So runstats is timed as the package returns it: mean `r fmt_ms(rs_main[["mean"]])` ms, sd `r fmt_ms(rs_main[["sd"]])` ms at w=`r w_mid` in the results tables. `r rs_txt` `r rs_agree_txt`
- **Deviation 5, argument choices the brief left open.** `RcppRoll::roll_medianr(fill = NA)` is used (right-aligned; plain `roll_median` is centred). The custom function is `sum_custom <- function(x) sum(x)`, a naive window sum (my reading of "unoptimised"; I did not have the post's exact body). Calls: `data.table::frollapply(x, n, sum_custom)` and `zoo::rollapply(x, n, sum_custom, fill = NA, align = "right")`.
- **Single-thread controls.** `data.table (1 thread)` is `setDTthreads(1)` for the cell (restored afterwards); `RcppRoll (1 thread)` is `options(RcppRoll.threads = 1)`; `roll (1 thread)` is `RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = 1)` (restored to `"auto"`). The one-thread entry of these three is timed right after its default-thread entry on the same data, through the same harness, and is also checked for correctness. The engines are ordered differently: each whole grid runs once per thread setting (all the DuckDB cells at the default threads, then all at one thread; then the polars grid in one fresh process at the default and in another at one thread), so an engine's default and one-thread cells are not neighbours. Thread settings as found, before any change: `OMP_NUM_THREADS` `r omp_env`, `getDTthreads()` `r n_dt_threads`, `RcppRoll::roll_threads()` `r n_rr_threads`, `RcppParallel::defaultNumThreads()` `r n_roll_threads` (`versions.csv`).
- **Correctness check (not in the post).** Results are computed outside timing, normalized (`as.numeric`, runstats shifted, left-pad with `NA`) and compared with `data.table::froll<stat>` via `all.equal(tolerance = tol)` (tol = `r tol_txt`) plus identical NA positions. cuplyr results are collected for this check only. A cell whose call errors counts as a failure in the table (it does not drop out of the count); `r if (n_err == 0) "there were none" else paste(words(n_err), "cell(s) errored")`.
- **Fallback check.** Every cuplyr cell is probed before it is timed: one untimed call under `options(cuplyr.fallback = "error")` (`rw_native_probe()` in `bench/rolling-lib.R`). A cell whose probe call falls back to the CPU (cuplyr's "fell back to CPU evaluation" error) is not timed, not checked for correctness and not plotted; it is recorded in the skipped-cells table below and in `skipped.csv`. A probe call that fails for any other reason is not a skip: in the main and extension experiments the cell is recorded as failed (an error row, which counts against the correctness total), and in the overhead, memory and fence chunks it stops the render. `r skip_count_txt` As a second check the timed cells catch `cuplyr_cpu_fallback` conditions: `r caught_txt`.
- **polars and DuckDB (F73).** Both are checked against data.table like every other entry, and both go through the same `run_cell()` and `rw_time()` as everything else (cold probe call, budgeted samples, gc before every call). DuckDB: an in-memory database (`shared_home = FALSE`, so nothing is written under the home directory) with the data loaded once into a real table by `dbWriteTable()` (not a re-scanned R data frame); one connection per (thread setting, dataset), with the default or `SET threads = 1`, each loading its dataset once outside timing and closed with `shutdown = TRUE` when its cells are done. A raw `ROWS` frame is partial at the start of the table (and of each group): it holds fewer than `n` rows and DuckDB aggregates them, where data.table gives NA, so the timed SQL guards the aggregate (`CASE WHEN i >= n`, with `row_number() OVER w` when grouped) and returns NULL until the window is full. The plain `CREATE TEMP TABLE` (no `OR REPLACE`) leaves the result inside DuckDB, and the `DROP TABLE` of the previous result runs untimed before every call (the `reset` hook of `run_cell()` and `rw_time()`, the probe call included); a drop inside timing would be an error, because the table would still exist. polars: the thread pool is fixed when polars first loads and is read from the environment variable `POLARS_MAX_THREADS`, so each polars configuration runs in its own fresh R process (`callr`, started by `rw_polars_child()`), with `POLARS_MAX_THREADS` set to one or unset before polars loads. That process puts `params$lib` first on its library path, sources the same `rolling-lib.R` this document sourced (by absolute path), never loads cuplyr (so it holds no CUDA context), runs its cells with the same harness, compares them with `rw_reference()` on the same seeded data and returns plain data frames. For both engines the thread count in effect is read back from the engine (`polars_info()$thread_pool_size`, `current_setting('threads')`), not assumed from the setting: `engine-threads.csv` has them (polars `r eng_default_thr[["polars"]]` by default and `r eng_one_thr[["polars"]]` at one thread; DuckDB `r eng_default_thr[["DuckDB"]]` and `r eng_one_thr[["DuckDB"]]`). The `custom` function has no polars or DuckDB entry (neither applies an R function over windows). No cuplyr CPU-fallback cell is timed, as before.
- cuplyr entries: `cuplyr` is native `roll_<stat>(x, n)` inside `mutate()`; `cuplyr (froll alias)` is `data.table::froll<stat>(x, n)` inside `mutate()` (cuplyr maps it to the same kernel; `r alias_txt`). `r median_entry_txt` Custom: n/a (cuplyr cannot apply an arbitrary R function over windows).
- **Comparison words.** Two medians are "level" when they are within `r fmt_pct(th_level, 0)` of each other, unless their interquartile ranges do not overlap, in which case one is "slightly faster" than the other; outside that band they are "faster" and "slower". A cost "grows" with the window width when the median at w=`r w_hi` is at least `r th_trend` times the median at w=`r w_lo` (it "shrinks" at the inverse ratio and is "flat" in between); slider is "growing" above `r th_grow` times. An entry "scales" with threads at a one-thread over default ratio of at least `r thr_yes`, and does not at `r thr_no` or less. Two figures "agree" within a factor of `r th_x` (so do the two pinned CPUs of one kind in chunk `bench-cores`, or that measurement counts as disturbed and none of its figures is quoted); a slow core is measurably slower above `r th_core` times; two calls "cost the same" within `r fmt_pct(th_same, 0)`; a custom function is clearly slower above `r th_avoid` times its optimized equivalent; the narrow-window call is "mostly call chain" when it is within `r fmt_pct(th_chain, 0)` of the `cumsum` mutate; a peak is "well inside" the card below `r fmt_pct(th_mem, 0)` of its memory. cuplyr's rank among the entries at their default settings (the one-thread controls are not ranked) is "near the front" when its rank divided by the number of those entries is at most `r th_front`, "near the back" at `r 1 - th_front` or more and "mid-pack" in between; the runstats alignment shift is "a sizeable part" of the mean figure when it adds more than `r fmt_pct(th_part, 0)` to it.

## Correctness

Every timed (statistic x function x width) cell, including every timed cuplyr entry, every one-thread control and every polars and DuckDB cell (`r n_eng_cells` of them, `r if (eng_cells_ok) "all" else "not all"` matching), was compared with data.table's result. Reference: `frollmean/frollmedian/frollmin/frollmax/frollsum/frollsd`, and `frollsum` for the custom sum.

`r n_ok` of `r n_cells` (function x width) cells match data.table (all.equal tol `r tol_txt`, same NA positions). The denominator counts the cells that were timed. `r denom_txt`

`r if (nrow(bad) == 0) "No cuplyr mismatch, and none for any other package." else sprintf("%s %s did not match; %s listed below.", cap1(words(nrow(bad))), plural(nrow(bad), "cell"), plural(nrow(bad), "it is", "they are"))` "Match" includes the leading `NA` padding after normalization (runstats after the right-alignment shift in `rw_normalize()`); a padding or sd-convention difference would have shown up as a mismatch. Not covered: data with `NA`s, `na.rm = TRUE`, non-default alignment.

**Edge semantics of polars and DuckDB.** Where an engine differs from data.table by definition, the benchmark either makes the result equal or keeps the difference out of what is compared:

- DuckDB's `ROWS BETWEEN n - 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` frame is partial at the start of the table (and of each group): it holds fewer than `n` rows, and DuckDB aggregates them where data.table has `NA`. The timed SQL guards the aggregate and returns NULL until the window is full, so the padding is the same as data.table's, and the check above compares it.
- polars returns null for an incomplete window, because `min_samples` defaults to the window size; the null positions are data.table's `NA` positions.
- The standard deviation is the sample standard deviation (`ddof = 1`) in all three: `STDDEV_SAMP`, `rolling_std` and `frollsd`.
- For an even window the median is the average of the two middle values in all three. Only odd widths are timed here (`r widths_slash`); the tests of the helpers in `bench/rolling-lib.R` check an even width as well.
- With `NA` in the input the engines differ: DuckDB's aggregates skip NULLs, so a window holding `NA`s still has a value once it holds enough non-null values (at least one for the mean, sum, min, max and median, at least two for the standard deviation), where polars and data.table give `NA` for any window that holds one. This data has no `NA`, so that difference is not exercised, and it would have to be handled before any comparison on data with missing values.

```{r}
#| label: correctness-bad
if (nrow(bad)) knitr::kable(bad[, c("stat", "fn", "width", "n_na_mismatch", "max_abs_diff", "note")], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Extension: where the GPU should help

Rolling mean, `r ext_times` samples per cell (`r if (all(ext$times == ext_times)) "no cuts" else sprintf("%s cells cut", sum(ext$times != ext_times))`). `peak_gpu_MB` is the peak from `cuplyr:::gpu_alloc_tracking()` around one untimed call; `held_after_MB` is what was still held when that call returned (see F1). `correct` compares with data.table's output. All cuplyr numbers here are computation only, data already on the GPU.

Two experiments: (a) grouped: `r grp_rows_txt` rows, `r groups_txt` interleaved groups, w = `r group_width`; (b) ungrouped: `r ext_txt` rows, w = `r widths_slash`.

```{r}
#| label: extension-table
ext_tab <- data.frame(
  experiment = ifelse(ext$experiment == "grouped mean", grp_lab, ung_lab), fn = ext$fn, width = ext$width, n_rows = fmt_rows(ext$n_rows),
  median_ms = fmt_ms(ext$median_ms), IQR = paste0(fmt_ms(ext$q25_ms), "-", fmt_ms(ext$q75_ms)), times = ext$times,
  peak_gpu_MB = ifelse(is.na(ext$peak_gpu_bytes), "", sprintf("%.0f", ext$peak_gpu_bytes / 1e6)),
  held_after_MB = ifelse(is.na(ext$held_gpu_bytes_after_call), "", sprintf("%.0f", ext$held_gpu_bytes_after_call / 1e6)),
  correct = ext$correct, note = ext$note, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ext_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: extension-plot
#| fig-height: !expr ext_plot_height
ext_plot()
```

cuplyr grouped is `group_by(tbl_gpu(df), g)` built outside timing, then `compute(mutate(gtg, r = roll_mean(x, n)))` plus the fence, with n the grouped width (`r group_width`). data.table is `dt[, r := frollmean(x, n), by = g]`, timed at the default thread setting and with `setDTthreads(1)`: **`r fmt_ms(g_dt1)` ms at one thread vs `r fmt_ms(g_dt)` ms by default, so its `by=` evaluation `r if (by_flat) "ran effectively single-threaded (it did not use the extra threads)" else "used threads"`**. slider is a grouped_df `mutate(r = slider::slide_mean(x, before = n - 1, complete = TRUE))`.

## Per-call cost breakdown (overhead)

Measured on the same harness as everything else (gc-separated, fenced, `compute()` of an eager `mutate()`), on a `r small_txt`-row table (kernel negligible; `r unique(oh$times[oh$n_rows == small_rows])[1]` samples) and, for contrast, on the `r rows_txt`-row table (`r unique(oh$times[oh$n_rows == n_rows & oh$stat == "overhead"])[1]` samples). The per-statistic `r small_txt`-row rolling floors are listed too.

```{r}
#| label: overhead-table
oh_all <- oh[oh$stat == "overhead" | oh$n_rows == small_rows, ]
oh_all$call <- ifelse(oh_all$stat == "overhead", oh_all$fn, paste0(oh_all$fn, " [", oh_all$stat, "]"))
oh_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(oh_all, list(oh_all$call, oh_all$n_rows), drop = TRUE), function(v)
  data.frame(call = v$call[1], rows = v$n_rows[1], median_ms_iqr = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt_ms(stats::median(v$ms)), fmt_ms(unname(stats::quantile(v$ms, .25))), fmt_ms(unname(stats::quantile(v$ms, .75)))),
             min_max_ms = sprintf("%s-%s", fmt_ms(min(v$ms)), fmt_ms(max(v$ms))), n = nrow(v), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
oh_tab <- oh_tab[order(oh_tab$rows, oh_tab$call), ]
oh_tab$rows <- fmt_int(oh_tab$rows)
knitr::kable(oh_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

- **The about-`r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms floor is for window-function mutates; a plain mutate is about `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms.** At `r small_txt` rows: plain `mutate(y = x + 1)` `r fmt_ms(plain_small)` ms, `mutate(r = cumsum(x))` `r ms_nt(cum_small)`, `mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n))` `r fmt_ms(roll_small)` ms (the `r words(length(floor_by_stat))` rolling statistics: `r range_num(floor_by_stat)` ms medians; all `r n_floor_samples` samples between `r fmt_ms(min(floor_df$ms))` and `r fmt_ms(max(floor_df$ms))` ms). `r cum_vs_roll_txt`
- **What the path does (read from the code, confirmed with `show_query()`).** A plain mutate is `r words(n_mat_plain)` `r plural(n_mat_plain, "node")` (`r code(chain_plain)`). An eager window mutate is `r code(chain_win)` (`R/mutate.R` lines `r ln_window`, `r ln_mutate` and `r ln_select` push the window, mutate and select nodes), and an eager call runs that chain as one execution (`push_chain()` in `R/execute.R`, F57): the nodes' outputs share the input table's columns instead of deep-copying them (`src/ops_window.cpp` about line `r ln_copy` passes the input columns through as shared pointers), so only the computed columns are allocated. Before F57 each node built a full table and `x` was copied `r times_word(n_mat_win)` per call. The per-node R work (node build, schema inference) is still done `r words(n_mat_win)` times; I did not profile where the `r fmt_1(win_extra)` ms goes at `r small_txt` rows.
**`r mem_lead`** (`r ext_txt` rows, `memory-breakdown.csv`):

```{r}
#| label: memory-table
mb_tab <- mem_breakdown
for (cn in setdiff(names(mb_tab), "call")) mb_tab[[cn]] <- fmt_int(mb_tab[[cn]])
if (nrow(mb_tab)) knitr::kable(mb_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

`r mem_txt`
**The `r alloc_part` cost scales with rows and is inside every `r rows_txt` and `r ext_txt` cuplyr timing.** At `r rows_txt` rows the plain mutate takes `r ms_nt(plain_big)``r ms_delta(plain_big, plain_small, paste(" vs", small_txt, "rows"))`, the `cumsum` window mutate `r ms_nt(cum_big)``r ms_delta(cum_big, cum_small)` and `roll_mean(x, n)` `r ms_nt(roll_big)``r ms_delta(roll_big, roll_small)`. The narrow-window rolling mean (w=`r w_lo`, `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_lo))` in the tables above) is `r narrow_txt`.`r if (!is.na(narrow_chain)) " (This is an inference from comparing two different kernels, not a profile.)" else ""`

With `RcppRoll.threads = 1` it takes `r rr1_list` ms `r rr1_ratio`. Against that one-thread RcppRoll, data.table`r dt_single_txt` compares as follows, with both at one thread: `r dt1_rr1_txt`. For the median, data.table at one thread takes `r dt1_med` ms (RcppRoll at one thread: `r rr1_med`); RollingWindow's median (`r rw_med` ms) compared with data.table at one thread is `r rw_med_txt`. `r dt_med_txt` `r exc_txt`

## Findings (candidate backlog rows; nothing was fixed in this feature)

- **F1 (`r f1_head`). Before F57 an eager window mutate materialized `r words(n_mat_win)` full tables and held them until R's GC.** One eager `mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n))` on `r ext_txt` rows runs `r code(paste(rev(plan_win[plan_win != "ast_source"]), collapse = " -> "))` (`R/mutate.R` `r ln_window`, `r ln_mutate`, `r ln_select`); in F54 each node built a new table and `src/ops_window.cpp` deep-copied every input column, so `x` was copied `r times_word(n_mat_win)`; F57 runs the chain once and shares the columns (`src/ops_window.cpp` about line `r ln_copy`). `r f1_meas_txt` `r f1_oom_lead`: `r f1_oom_txt`.`r f1_tail`
- **F2. `r f2_lead`** At `r rows_txt` rows, from w=`r w_mid` to w=`r w_hi`, mean goes from `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_mid))` to `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_hi))` and sd from `r ms_nt(med("sd", "cuplyr", w_mid))` to `r ms_nt(med("sd", "cuplyr", w_hi))` (data.table is `r trend("sd", "data.table")` in the width: `r fmt_ms(med("sd", "data.table", w_hi))` ms for sd at w=`r w_hi`). At `r ext_txt` rows mean at w=`r w_hi` takes `r ms_nt(u_hi("cuplyr"))` for cuplyr vs data.table `r fmt_ms(u_hi("data.table"))` and `r lab_cpu("RcppRoll")` `r fmt_ms(u_hi("RcppRoll"))`. `r f2_infer` `r f2_row_if`: an incremental mean/sum (prefix sums) and a Welford or sum-of-squares sd, checked against `all.equal()` at the correctness tolerance (`r tol_txt`), or find a cudf aggregation that does not rescan each window (needs a probe).
- **F3. `r f3_lead`** `r f3_body`
- **F4. A fixed overhead of about `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms per eager window-function `mutate()` on a `r small_txt`-row table (`r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms for a plain mutate).** About `r fmt_1(win_extra)` ms of the `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` is specific to the window path, i.e. the `r chain_win` chain (`r f4_chain_txt`; `cumsum` costs `r ms_nt(cum_small)` against `r ms_nt(roll_small)` for `roll_mean`), `r kernel_txt`; the rest is the `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms every eager mutate pays. At `r rows_txt` rows the same chain costs `r ms_nt(cum_big)` for `cumsum` against `r ms_nt(plain_big)` for a plain mutate`r f4_share_txt`. `r f4_row_txt`
- **F5 (minor). No documented completion semantics.** `r f5_sync`, so wall-clock timing of cuplyr from R is only meaningful after a wait; the benchmark uses `gpu_sync()` as its fence (F57 added it; before, a one-row `gpu_head()` read did the job). Related: `x$ptr` on a `tbl_gpu` from outside the namespace `r ptr_txt`.

## How to render

```{r}
#| label: render-time
# How long this render took, and which timing chunks ran in it. A cached timing
# chunk comes back with the start time of the render that ran it, so a chunk ran
# in this render when it started at or after this render's start (chunk_ran, in
# the data chunk). Only a render in which every timing chunk ran is a complete
# cold render. It writes render-time.csv (the cache key, the md5 of the timing
# chunks' code and each chunk's start time), so a later warm render whose cached
# results all come from that render can still say what a cold render took (and
# bench/rolling-window.R adds the Quarto and pandoc total to that record).
render_end <- Sys.time()
render_secs <- as.numeric(difftime(render_end, render_t0, units = "secs"))
# rt_path, rt and rt_ok come from the data chunk: the record is this code's only
# when its cache key, its code key and the start times of the cached chunks match
if (all(chunk_ran)) {
  utils::write.csv(data.frame(key = cache_key, code_key = bench_code_key,
                              render_start = format(render_t0, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                              render_end = format(render_end, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                              start_epoch = sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(render_t0)), end_epoch = sprintf("%.3f", as.numeric(render_end)),
                              chunk_starts = chunk_starts_txt, knit_secs = render_secs,
                              timing_secs = wall_secs, total_secs = NA_real_, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                   rt_path, row.names = FALSE)
}
n_chunks <- length(chunk_ran)
render_rest_txt <- if (all(chunk_ran)) {
  sprintf(", of which the timing chunks took %s. Every timing chunk ran in this render, so it is a complete cold render of this code, from %s",
          fmt_dur(wall_secs), rt_span(format(render_t0, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), format(render_end, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")))
} else {
  last_cold <- if (rt_ok) sprintf("The last complete cold render of this code took %s (knitting, from %s%s), of which the timing chunks took %s.",
                                  fmt_dur(rt$knit_secs), rt_span(rt$render_start, rt$render_end),
                                  if (is.na(rt$total_secs)) "" else sprintf("; %s with Quarto and pandoc included", fmt_dur(rt$total_secs)),
                                  fmt_dur(rt$timing_secs)) else
    sprintf("The time of a complete cold render of this code is not known: %s.",
            if (!rt_have) "there is no `render-time.csv` next to the output (a render in which every timing chunk ran writes it)" else
              if (!rt_key_ok) "the `render-time.csv` next to the output records a render with another cache key (other helper or cuplyr code, versions or parameters)" else
                if (!rt_code_ok) sprintf("the `render-time.csv` next to the output records the cold render from %s, but the code of a timing chunk has changed since", rt_span(rt$render_start, rt$render_end)) else
                  sprintf("the `render-time.csv` next to the output records the cold render from %s, but not every cached timing result comes from that render", rt_span(rt$render_start, rt$render_end)))
  if (!any(chunk_ran)) {
    paste0(sprintf(" and ran none of the timing chunks: all %s were cache hits, so none of their time is part of this render. ", words(n_chunks)), last_cold)
  } else {
    sprintf(", of which the timing chunks that ran in it (%s) took %s; the other %s (%s) were cache hits, so this is not a complete cold render and its time is not the time of one. %s",
            join_and(names(chunk_ran)[chunk_ran]), fmt_dur(sum(secs_by_chunk[chunk_ran])), words(sum(!chunk_ran)),
            join_and(names(chunk_ran)[!chunk_ran]), last_cold)
  }
}
# the sentence in the text closes with its own full stop
render_rest_txt <- sub("\\.$", "", render_rest_txt)
```

This render took `r fmt_dur(render_secs)` (knitting, from the setup chunk to the last chunk)`r render_rest_txt`. The report is published at `r file.path(params$out_dir, "rolling-window.html")`.

Render only through `tools/r`, because the benchmark holds the GPU and the project has one GPU lock for every R process. From the checkout:

```
tools/r 'source("bench/rolling-window.R")'
```

That runs `quarto render` on this file with `params$root` set to the checkout, writes `rolling-window.html` and the CSVs to `params$out_dir` and keeps the knitr cache of the `bench-*` chunks in `params$cache_dir`. Quarto empties the directory given to `--output-dir` before it renders, and `params$out_dir` holds the install logs this document reads (and, by default, the cache), so the wrapper renders into a temporary directory and copies the HTML over. Do the same by hand: never pass `params$out_dir` as `--output-dir`. `r cold_work_txt`; a render with a warm cache re-renders only the prose, tables and figures and takes seconds. A render in which every timing chunk ran also writes `render-time.csv` to `params$out_dir` (the cache key, a hash of the timing chunks' code, the start and end of the render, the start time of each timing chunk, its knitting time and the time of the timing chunks; `bench/rolling-window.R` adds the total with Quarto and pandoc), so that a later warm render can still say what a cold render took. A warm render quotes that record only when the cache key and the code of the timing chunks are unchanged and every cached result started inside that render at the time the record gives for it; after a timing chunk is edited and rerun, the record is not quoted. Quarto `r quarto_ver` is used; it is a user install and is not installed or upgraded by anything here.

To try it at smoke size (a few seconds), put the overrides in a YAML file and render this file in place with `--execute-params`; the keys are the front matter's `params`, and with the output and cache directories under `/tmp` the default cache is left alone:

```
root: "/path/to/the/checkout"
out_dir: "/tmp/rolling-out"
cache_dir: "/tmp/rolling-cache"
n_rows: 5000
times: 2
times_custom: 1
cell_budget: 1
probe_limit: 5
group_rows: 5000
n_groups: 10
ext_rows: 20000
ext_times: 2
```

```
tools/r 'system2(Sys.which("quarto"), c("render", "bench/rolling-window.qmd", "--output-dir", "/tmp/rolling-html", "--execute-params", "smoke.yml"))'
```

The test `tests/testthat/test-parity-F63-qmd-render.R` does the same on a copy of this file in a temporary directory, with a clean cache, a prose-only edit, a code edit, an edit of the helper file and a forced rerun in turn (opt in with `CUPLYR_BENCH_RENDER=1`).

**Forcing a full rerun.** Set `FULL_RERUN <- TRUE` before `source("bench/rolling-window.R")`; it passes `-P rebuild:true`, which makes the setup chunk set `cache.rebuild` for the `bench-*` chunks, so every timing chunk runs again and saves its cache anew (`rebuild` is not part of the cache key). Do the same by hand with `-P rebuild:true` (or `rebuild: true` in the parameters file), or delete the cache directory (`r params$cache_dir`). Do not use `quarto render --cache-refresh`. In a review probe it re-ran none of the timing chunks, switched caching on for every other chunk, the setup chunk included, and left cache and figure directories next to the source; a later render would then restore the setup chunk from that cache instead of running it (reasoned, not run).

**What invalidates the cache.** A `bench-*` chunk reruns when any of these change: the chunk's own code or options; the content (not the modification time) of `bench/rolling-lib.R`; the content of cuplyr's `R/*.R` and `src/*.{cpp,cu,cuh,h,hpp}` files and of `src/Makevars` (the compile flags) under `params$root`; the version of R, of libcudf (`r cudf_ver`), of polars' Rust crate (`r polars_crate`) or of any package the benchmark uses (`r join_and(code(names(ver)[names(ver) != "R"]))`); or any run parameter other than the directories and the rebuild switch (`root`, `out_dir`, `cache_dir`, `rebuild`). Prose, tables and figures are never cached, so editing them never reruns a benchmark. The cached chunks return plain data frames only: a GPU object left in a cached chunk would be restored as a dead pointer.
